title: Calendar
content:
# Calendar

List Outlook calendars and events, create and update events with Microsoft Teams meetings, RSVP to invitations, and find free time across mailboxes.

Every call takes the `accountId` of a Microsoft account connected with `scopes=calendar`. Times are ISO 8601 with an offset, and event ids are Microsoft Graph ids.

## List calendars

`GET /v1/calendar/calendars?accountId=…` returns the user's Outlook calendars, with `primary`, `timezone` and `readOnly` for each. Use an `id` from it as `calendarId`, or `primary` for the user's main calendar.

## List events

`GET /v1/calendar/events` returns the events between `from` and `to`, both required:

```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/calendar/events?accountId=ACCOUNT_ID&from=2026-11-02T00:00:00Z&to=2026-11-09T00:00:00Z" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "AAMkAGI2…",
      "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID",
      "provider": "microsoft",
      "calendarId": "primary",
      "title": "Kickoff",
      "start": "2026-11-03T10:00:00+01:00",
      "end": "2026-11-03T10:30:00+01:00",
      "allDay": false,
      "participants": [{ "email": "client@example.com", "status": "accepted" }],
      "conferencing": { "provider": "teams", "url": "https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meetup-join/…" },
      "status": "confirmed",
      "htmlLink": "https://outlook.office365.com/owa/?itemid=…"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": { "hasMore": false, "nextCursor": null }
}
```

| Parameter | What it does |
|-----------|--------------|
| `calendarId` | The calendar to read. Default `primary` |
| `expandRecurring` | Returns each occurrence of a recurring event. Default `true`; `false` returns the series |
| `showCancelled` | Includes cancelled events. Default `false` |
| `title`, `location`, `icalUid` | Narrow the results. `title` and `location` are applied to the fetched page |
| `timezone` | IANA name for the returned times |
| `sortOrder`, `cursor`, `limit` | `asc` by default; up to 200 per page, default 50 |

The window between `from` and `to` can be at most 400 days. A wider one answers `400` with the number of days you sent.

Outlook expands every recurring series across the window, so keep polling windows narrow.

When Outlook is slow, a page can hold fewer events than `limit` plus a `nextCursor`. Pass it as `cursor` to continue.

A first page that stalls is read a second time.

If Outlook still does not answer, you get the last list from the past six hours with `stale: true` and `asOf`, or a `502` when there is none.

For a window wider than 31 days, the `502` becomes a partial list around today. See [When a wide window is too heavy](/products/calendar#when-a-wide-window-is-too-heavy).

With `expandRecurring=false`, the list includes series that started before `from` and still recur in the window, and any event that overlaps its edges.

## Create an event

`POST /v1/calendar/events` creates the event and sends invitations to the participants. Set `conferencing` to `teams` to attach a Teams meeting:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/calendar/events" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID",
    "title": "Demo call",
    "start": "2026-11-04T15:00:00+01:00",
    "end": "2026-11-04T15:30:00+01:00",
    "participants": [{ "email": "client@example.com", "name": "Client" }],
    "conferencing": "teams",
    "reminders": { "useDefault": false, "overrides": [{ "method": "popup", "minutes": 10 }] }
  }'
```

| Field | What it does |
|-------|--------------|
| `calendarId` | The calendar to create it on. Default `primary` |
| `title` | Required, up to 1,000 characters |
| `start`, `end` | ISO 8601 with an offset, or a `YYYY-MM-DD` date with `allDay: true` |
| `timezone` | IANA name for the event. Default: the mailbox's working-hours zone, or UTC on personal accounts |
| `participants` | Up to 100, as `{ email, name?, optional?, resource? }`. `resource` books a room or equipment address |
| `recurrence` | One RRULE with `FREQ` `DAILY`, `WEEKLY`, `MONTHLY` or `YEARLY`, and `INTERVAL`, `COUNT`, `UNTIL`, `BYDAY`, `BYSETPOS` or `WKST`, plus `EXDATE` lines. Outlook has no EXDATE, so Zernio deletes those occurrences after saving |
| `reminders` | `{ useDefault, overrides }`. Outlook keeps one popup reminder, the first override. An override with `method: "email"` answers `400` `reminder_method_unsupported` |
| `conferencing` | `teams` |
| `description`, `location`, `busy`, `visibility` | `visibility` is `default`, `public` or `private` |
| `metadata` | String pairs kept on the event |

`PATCH /v1/calendar/events/{eventId}` takes the same fields, and `DELETE /v1/calendar/events/{eventId}?accountId=…` deletes the event. Outlook emails the participants on every change, so `notifyParticipants` only accepts `all` here. A `PATCH` that moves an event without `timezone` keeps the event's zone.

## Edit a recurring series

Every event has a `type`: `single`, `series` for a recurring master, `occurrence` for one of its instances, or `exception` for an instance changed on its own.

Occurrences carry `masterEventId` and `originalStart`, their slot in the pattern.

`GET /v1/calendar/events/{eventId}/instances?accountId=…&from=…&to=…` lists a series' occurrences in a window, with the same `cursor` and `limit` as event lists:

```bash
curl "https://zernio.com/api/v1/calendar/events/SERIES_ID/instances?accountId=ACCOUNT_ID&from=2026-11-01T00:00:00Z&to=2026-12-01T00:00:00Z" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY"
```

- To change one occurrence, `PATCH` or `DELETE` its own `id`.
- To change the whole series, `PATCH` the series id. A new `recurrence` makes Outlook drop earlier changes to single occurrences.
- For "this and all following", end the series with `UNTIL` in its `recurrence`, then create a new series from that date.

## Answer an invitation

`POST /v1/calendar/events/{eventId}/rsvp` sets the mailbox's response, with an optional note to the organizer:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/calendar/events/EVENT_ID/rsvp" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID", "status": "accepted", "comment": "See you there" }'
```

`status` is `accepted`, `declined` or `tentative`. Outlook sends the answer and the note to the organizer, unless you send `"sendResponse": false`.

## Check free-busy

`POST /v1/calendar/free-busy` returns the busy blocks of up to 10 connected mailboxes, Microsoft and Google mixed, between `from` and `to`:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/calendar/free-busy" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "accountIds": ["ACCOUNT_ID_1", "ACCOUNT_ID_2"], "from": "2026-11-02T08:00:00Z", "to": "2026-11-02T18:00:00Z" }'
```

```json
{ "data": [{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID_1", "from": "2026-11-02T08:00:00Z", "to": "2026-11-02T18:00:00Z", "busy": [{ "start": "2026-11-02T09:00:00Z", "end": "2026-11-02T10:00:00Z" }], "calendars": [{ "id": "primary", "busy": [{ "start": "2026-11-02T09:00:00Z", "end": "2026-11-02T10:00:00Z" }] }], "people": [] }] }
```

`busy` merges every calendar read. To choose calendars or check coworkers who never connected, send `accounts` instead of `accountIds`:

```json
{ "accounts": [{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID_1", "calendarIds": ["primary"], "emails": ["ada@yourcompany.com"] }], "from": "2026-11-02T08:00:00Z", "to": "2026-11-02T18:00:00Z" }
```

Coworkers come back in `people`. An account that cannot be read gets `busy: null` and an `error`, and the other accounts still answer.

## Find a meeting time

`POST /v1/calendar/availability` turns free-busy into bookable slots for up to 10 participants:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://zernio.com/api/v1/calendar/availability" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ZERNIO_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "participants": [{ "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID_1" }, { "accountId": "ACCOUNT_ID_2" }],
    "from": "2026-11-02T00:00:00Z",
    "to": "2026-11-06T00:00:00Z",
    "durationMinutes": 30,
    "defaultOpenHours": [{ "days": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5], "timezone": "Europe/Madrid", "start": "09:00", "end": "17:00" }]
  }'
```

```json
{ "data": { "timeSlots": [{ "from": "2026-11-02T08:00:00.000Z", "to": "2026-11-02T08:30:00.000Z", "accountIds": ["ACCOUNT_ID_1", "ACCOUNT_ID_2"] }] } }
```

| Field | What it does |
|-------|--------------|
| `participants` | 1 to 10, each `{ accountId, openHours? }` |
| `durationMinutes` | Slot length, 5 to 480 |
| `intervalMinutes` | Step between slot starts, 5 to 240. Default 30 |
| `roundTo` | Rounds `from` up to a multiple of 5 to 60 minutes |
| `buffer` | `{ before, after }` minutes of padding around existing meetings, up to 240 each |
| `defaultOpenHours`, `openHours` | Working hours: `days` (0 is Sunday), `timezone`, `start` and `end` as `HH:MM`, and optional `exdates` |
| `method` | `collective` (default): everyone is free. `max_availability`: slots where any participant is free, with who in `accountIds` |

## How it behaves

- Get, update, delete and RSVP by event id work on any of the user's own calendars. Pass `calendarId` (query on `GET` and `DELETE`, body on `PATCH` and RSVP) to reach an event on a calendar shared with the user.
- Free-busy and availability read each mailbox's schedule in 15-minute steps. Named `calendarIds` are read from their events instead. Working elsewhere counts as free.
- Coworkers in `emails` are read through Outlook's schedule lookup, up to 19 per mailbox, on work and school accounts only.
- Creates, updates and deletes email the participants, as Outlook does.
- `calendar.event.created`, `calendar.event.updated` and `calendar.event.deleted` fire for changes on the primary calendar. See [Webhooks](/platforms/microsoft/webhooks).

## If it fails

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|-------|-------|-----|
| `400` `invalid_field_value`, `param: conferencing` | `google_meet` on a Microsoft account | Use `teams`. |
| `400` `unsupported_for_provider`, `param: notifyParticipants` | `external` or `none` on a Microsoft account | Omit it; Outlook always notifies. |
| `400` on `recurrence` | More than one rule, `RDATE` or `EXRULE`, or an unsupported part | Send one RRULE with the supported parts, plus any `EXDATE` lines. |
| `404` `resource_not_found` | The event was deleted, or the id is wrong | List the events again. |
| `412` `account_scope_missing` | The account has no `calendar` area | [Connect again](/platforms/microsoft/connect#add-areas-later) with `calendar` in `scopes`. |
